title: Register engine arguments as tuning parameters
description:
Registers dials tuning parameters for engine arguments with `parsnip::set_model_arg()`.

**`tabular_resnet()`, `tabular_rln()`, `tabular_auto_int()`, `tabular_saint()` (brulee):**

- The learning-rate scheduler arguments that brulee passes through `...` to `set_learn_rate()`: `initial` (`rate_initial()`), `largest` (`rate_largest()`), `reduction` (`rate_reduction()`), `steps` (`rate_steps()`), `step_size` (`rate_step_size()`), `decay` (`rate_decay()`).

**`tabular_pfn()` (tabpfn):** `training_set_limit` (`training_set_limit()`).

**`tabular_icl()` (brulee):** `normalization` (`normalization()`), `training_set_limit` (`training_set_limit()`).

**Caveat:** each scheduler argument only applies to some `rate_schedule` values. If one is tuned alongside a schedule that doesn't use it, the fit errors; brulee `mlp()` has the same limitation.

The brulee `tabular_pfn` engine registration for `training_set_limit` was added directly to the `brulee-pfn` branch.


The validation-set proportion (`validation`) is intentionally not registered as a tuning parameter.

title: Makes mocks more tolerant to argument changes of deps
description:
Makes mocked functions from `brulee` and `tabicl` more resilient to API changes. It does that by making the mocked functions rely on `...` as much as possible, but careful to keep those arguments that the tests use as explicitly defined. Here is the breakdown of what was changed:

| # | Mock | Helper | Inputs read by the mock | Proposed signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `chronos2_download()` | `helper-chronos.R` | `revision` (by name) | `function(..., revision)` | |
| 2 | `chronos2_parse_config()` | `helper-chronos.R` | None | `function(...)` | |
| 3 | `chronos2_model()` | `helper-chronos.R` | None | `function(...)` | Stored `config` is never read back; drop it from the fake object |
| 4 | `load_chronos2_weights()` | `helper-chronos.R` | None | `function(...)` | Also removes the `path` vs `safetensors_path` drift |
| 5 | `chronos2_predict_core()` | `helper-chronos.R` | `object`, `context` (by position); `prediction_length` (by name) | `function(object, context, ..., prediction_length = NULL)` | Only mocked when `also_mock_predict_core = TRUE` |
| 6 | `$.fake_chronos_module()` | `helper-chronos.R` | `x`, `name` | No change | S3 method, not a mocked binding; signature fixed by the `$` generic |
| 7 | `tabicl_cache_lookup()` | `helper-icl.R` | None | `function(...)` | |
| 8 | `tabicl_parse_config()` | `helper-icl.R` | `path` (by position) | `function(path, ...)` | |
| 9 | `tabicl_load_model()` | `helper-icl.R` | None | `function(...)` | Stored `task` is never read back; drop it from the fake object |
| 10 | `tabicl_classifier_proba()` | `helper-icl.R` | `y_train`, `x_test` (3rd and 4th by position) | `function(loaded, x_train, y_train, x_test, ...)` | |
| 11 | `tabicl_regressor_mean()` | `helper-icl.R` | `y_train`, `x_test` (3rd and 4th by position) | Replace with `tabicl_regressor_stats()` mock | Dead: brulee's predict now calls `tabicl_regressor_stats()`, so the TabICL regression test fails |

title: Adds tests, some bug fixes found during developing the tests
description:
## Summary

Adds a full test suite (parsnip-style) bringing `tabular` to 100% line coverage, fixes the bugs that surfaced while writing the tests, and updates the coverage CI so it actually exercises the torch engines.

## Bug fixes

- **`multi_predict()` never worked for resnet or auto_int.** resnet's method was registered under the wrong S3 class (`_torch_resnet`) so it never dispatched, and both methods called `predict()` on the wrong object with the wrong epoch argument. Now they dispatch and return per-epoch predictions.
- **`epochs = NULL` errored** in rln/auto_int/resnet `multi_predict()`. The default was `length(estimates)`, one past the end (brulee indexes `estimates[[epoch + 1]]`), giving `subscript out of bounds`. Changed to `length(estimates) - 1L`.
- **Removed `class_only()`/`prob_only()`** — helper functions that were defined but never connected to pfn's prediction setup (dead code).

## Tests

A test file per model. Each one covers:

- **Spec creation** — the model object builds with the right defaults (mode, engine, class).
- **Argument capture** — values passed to the model function are stored on the spec.
- **`update()`** — changing a spec's arguments after it's created, including `fresh = TRUE` (drop the old arguments instead of merging).
- **`check_args()`** — invalid argument values raise the expected errors (recorded as snapshots).
- **`required_pkgs()`** — the model reports the packages it needs.
- **Registration** — the model is registered with parsnip (`show_engines()` returns its engine/modes).
- **Fit & predict** — fitting against the real engine and predicting, including `multi_predict()` (predictions at several epochs).

New test files for pfn, resnet, and grids.

**Registering models for coverage.** Each model registers itself with parsnip inside `.onLoad()` (via a `make_*()` function). covr can't attribute `.onLoad` code to any test, so all that registration code reads as uncovered. The new `reregister_model()` test helper removes a model from parsnip's registry (`parsnip::get_model_env()`) so a test can call `make_*()` again and actually exercise it. (parsnip itself sidesteps this differently — it registers its built-in models with top-level code in `*_data.R` files, which covr *does* count, and never clears/re-registers a model in its own tests.)

Result: **coverage 21.5% → 100%.**

## CI

The coverage workflow now sets `NOT_CRAN: true` (so the `skip_on_cran()` engine tests run) and installs + **caches** the torch backend via `TORCH_INSTALL: 1` and a cached `TORCH_HOME`. Without this the torch-gated tests skip and Codecov under-reports (~95%).

## Housekeeping

- Renamed `R/auto_int.R` → `R/tabular_auto_int.R` (matches the function, the other model files, and its test).

## Notes

- 100% coverage requires `NOT_CRAN=true` **and** an installed torch backend; the CI change handles both. Locally: `withr::with_envvar(c(NOT_CRAN = "true"), devtools::test_coverage())`.
- Filed [brulee#122](https://github.com/tidymodels/brulee/issues/122): resnet predicts all-`NA` when the trailing training batch has 1 row. Not blocking — tests size data to avoid that case.

title: Adds support for Chronos2
description:
### New: 
   - R/tabular_chronos.R
   - tests/testthat/helper-chronos.R (contains infrastructure for the mocked tests)
   - tests/testthat/test-tabular_chronos.R

### New methodology

- **Quantile regression mode** — first model to register "quantile regression", the type = "quantile" prediction, and hardhat::quantile_pred output. quantile_levels is set once via set_mode("quantile regression", quantile_levels = ...) and auto-forwarded to the fit through defaults = list(quantile_levels = rlang::expr(quantile_levels)) — the same mechanism linear_reg() + quantreg uses for tau. (Also registers "regression" mode for the median point forecast.)
- **Forecasting predict semantics** — first model whose prediction row count is the forecast horizon (prediction_length), deliberately not one row per new_data row.
- **Zero main arguments** — first wrapper with no set_model_arg()/dials linkage. All forecast config (prediction_length, id_column, timestamp_column, model_id, revision, device, cache_dir) is supplied as engine args via set_engine().
- **Mocked end-to-end tests** — first use of a helper-*.R + testthat::local_mocked_bindings. stub_chronos_loaders() (ported from brulee) mocks the download/build/inference path so fit() + predict() run deterministically with no ~500MB download, gated only by torch availability + skip_on_cran().
- **Single-series enforcement** — the parsnip interface forecasts one series; chronos_single_series() errors (pointing to brulee::brulee_chronos()) if a multi-series id column appears, rather than silently dropping it. Documented in @details.

### Incidental changes

- Added robodev to ignores files (let me know if you'd like me to remove)

title: Updates parameter handling
description:
- **Removed 11 local parameter definitions** (`R/param_*.R`) now provided by dials: `bottleneck_units`, `dropout_attn`, `dropout_embedding`, `num_attn_blocks`, `num_attn_feat`, `num_attn_heads`, `num_embedding`, `penalty_average`, `penalty_type`, `resid_at`, `step_rate` — along with their tests and man pages. Verified field-by-field that the dials definitions are identical (type / range / `inclusive` / `trans` / `values`).

- **Repointed `set_model_arg()` registrations** from `pkg = "tabular"` → `pkg = "dials"` across `auto_int.R`, `tabular_rln.R`, and `tabular_resnet.R`.

- **Fixed a pre-existing bug:** `resid_at` had no `set_model_arg()` registration, so it was silently dropped before reaching 
brulee and was invisible to `tune()`. Added the registration, mapping the parsnip arg `resid_at` → brulee's engine arg `residual_at`.

- **Re-pointed roxygen autolinks** in `tabular_rln.R` to `[dials::penalty_average()]` / `[dials::step_rate()]` to avoid dangling-link check warnings.

- **DESCRIPTION:** `dials (>= 1.4.3.9000)`, dropped now-unused `scales`, added `brulee (>= 0.7.0)` to Suggests (all four engine functions tabular uses are new in brulee 0.7.0), and added `Remotes: tidymodels/brulee, tidymodels/dials` since both are dev-only for now.
